title: Telegram to Sun Yat-sen, Swatow to Tokyo, 3 April 1916 (JACAR B03050738800)

plaintext.source: The Japanese Foreign Ministry could not read it; the file holds no solution.

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's transcription checked against the JACAR PDF (600 dpi render of frame 0296)
transcription.notes: 177 code letters per NOTES; no ciphertext file to measure. Four letters corrected on the image (gedocijiga, xitonatula, kufonemige, baxuxepeja).

system.summary: Standard Chinese telegraph code condensed to consonant-vowel syllables by a systematic table (20 consonants rotated to l, vowels e a i o u, column-major 01-00), no additive.
system.sibling_key: Same family as Yamada Junzaburō's two published condenser tables; used to define the search family.
system.notes: Ten letters (five syllables, two codes) per word; 46 of 50 distinct syllables confirmed.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's attempts with the Yamada tables negative (blog 12 Dec 2021)

solution.what: Syllable statistics: Yamada's 20 consonants, rare u pointing to a vowel-major table.
Brute force of the systematic condenser family scored by a Chinese character LM; winner 49 points clear.
Four doubtful codes fixed by sense and confirmed in the handwriting; content matches Mo Qingyu's March 1916 rising.
Tail checked on a 600 dpi render: the garble is the operator's; three characters unrecoverable.

Tail re-examined as a Morse transmission slip (the received sheet is clean, so the errors are the telegraph's): p (.--.) = a (.-) + n (-.) with the letter space lost, so ropezpo = ro pe za no = 返港 'returns to Hong Kong'. A Morse re-division search (morse_tail.py) of zpo gives four valid codes at one space change (港, 砉, 彼, 嫗); only 港 fits. The last word ngobunibai gives no sensible decoding with up to four space changes; 翼□ (5068) one-letter and one-element Morse slips give no word or known name.

Outside check of the sibling intercepts (sunintercepts page; not the Swatow sheet). Brice Dudout re-read our March-May 1916 condenser transcriptions on the JACAR scans. Of 47 transcribed g he checked, 30 are q on the form, because this copyist's q has its loop on the right. Of our 21 emendations, 19 are already correct on the form, so they were the model's misreadings, not clerk slips. Our 3 Apr 1916 transcription had left out a whole word. Confirmed here on our own PDFs: 0489a gyrobatapo (b, not our t); 0416b xodugoluro (x, not our r); 0416b qiheyuxifa (q, not g), settled by the twin 0416a, transcribed here and decoded in his six-vowel grid with no emendation, which ends 確否速示俾便行止; and the omitted word jobusosuji (088300 fr. 0489), which realigns the 3 Apr tail to 已澈查局非誣騙. His full list of 28 corrections is not yet checked item by item.

March 1917 forms (B03050090200 fr. 0504-0507) re-examined after the 1916 finding. 23 Mar: our transcription had left out two whole words, macorarala veyurojiji, so the 'clerk's lacuna' was partly ours. 22 code words now, matching the form, and about nine codes after 妥 are still unread. 26 Mar: the form has Qeta (capital Q) and zahu (h), so the emendations g->q and k->h were misreadings. 25 Mar: zubo's z has the clerk's x shape. The other 1917 emendations are not rechecked.

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): this profile is the Swatow telegram of 3 Apr 1916 and its one condenser key. The credits for other keys were taken off it: Brice Dudout's decipherment of the July-November 1916 systems and his transcription corrections (y1916, sibling intercepts, not the Swatow sheet), and wanglu2016's issue #23 identifications (1917 telegrams, y1917). They stay credited in y1916/NOTES.md, y1917/NOTES.md and on the sunintercepts page, which has no profile of its own yet.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Tomokiyo's transcription and the Chinese/English decipherment copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/; decode_out.txt (decode.py output, codes and the recovered condenser table) linked as decryption and key

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): the text is Chinese; not scorable by the word lists; read by the reader (one unread character, last word garbled). Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

validation.notes: plaintext is Chinese (telegraph code); no letter model

outcome.method_basis: The condenser table (20 consonants rotated to start at l, vowels e a i o u, numbered column-major) was deduced from the ciphertext by analogy with Yamada's known tables, then read through the standard Chinese telegraph code; Tomokiyo's attempts with Yamada's own tables had failed.
outcome.notes: 42 of about 44 characters (港 restored from a Morse slip, M, 30 Sept 2026); the last word, about two codes, is garbled in the received copy; 翼□ second character unresolved.

credits.note: transcription of the Swatow telegram (frame 680682), checked on the image

texts.label: Swatow to 'Rosamonde Tokio', 3 Apr 1916 (JACAR B03050738800)
texts.summary: A telegram signed 'Tanaka' from Swatow to Sun Yat-sen's household in Tokyo, intercepted by the Japanese Foreign Ministry, which could not read it. It reports that Mo Qingyu declared Chaozhou independent against Yuan Shikai, that Sun's men recovered Swatow, and that Mo then came with a large force and ordered them out of the garrison headquarters.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): the text is Chinese; the sweep scored the English gloss as English. The word lists cannot score Chinese; read by the reader: five sentences, one unread character (翼□) and the last word garbled, 港 restored from a Morse slip (grade M). Sentences hold. Keeps read.

texts.label: “Shanghai” table: 36 telegrams read by Brice Dudout (31 July 1914 - 25 April 1916)
texts.summary: Shanghai ↔ Tokyo (“Rosamonde”, Yamada Junzaburō), June 1915–April 1916. Table published by D. Bourdeau. Also attested from Changchun on 31 July 1914.

reading_review.note: 36 telegrams; the first 22 (0121-0495, Feb-Apr 1916: Takano diet, Second Squadron, Morrison plan, funds) read at A level, but the 14 April 1916 word-count telegrams 0557-0636b are dense fragments (20-40% doubtful, e.g. 0557, 0568b, 0580, 0601b, 0617, 0631b; repeated phrases in 0580 and 0617) that only partly build sentences; the translation marks the gaps honestly.

texts.label: “Yamada” table — “Thirtyseventh”: 29 telegrams read by Brice Dudout (3 May 1916 - 21 June 1916)
texts.summary: Tokyo ↔ Shanghai (“Junzaburo”, “Linwailuk”), May–June 1916; clear indicator “Thirtyseventh” on most. Table published by D. Bourdeau.

reading_review.note: 29 telegrams (Xie Chi to Shanghai, May-June 1916: Shandong campaign, Tianjin students, military notes, aircraft), coherent; 64 of 1385 codes doubtful, a few unmarked slips (懷仁描事, 軍譚五百, 小達六十); translation follows closely.

texts.label: “Qingdao” table: 19 telegrams read by Brice Dudout (19 March 1916 - 26 April 1916)
texts.summary: Qingdao ↔ Tokyo (Ju Zheng, Kayano Nagatomo), March–April 1916. Table published by D. Bourdeau.

reading_review.note: 19 telegrams, 131 of 636 doubtful; 0394-0492 and 0008 read cleanly, 0568a, 0602b, 0607a, 0614, 0615, 0625b partly, but 0559b, 0560b, 0604b, 0635a, 0636a, 0642a are mostly doubtful fragments; translation largely gaps there.

texts.label: “Manila” table: 8 telegrams read by Brice Dudout (6 January 1915 - 3 May 1916)
texts.summary: Tokyo ↔ Manila, March 1916. Table published by D. Bourdeau.

reading_review.note: 8 telegrams, coherent (Tan Gen's aircraft, the suspicious use of the code, bonds and medals); 0566 is the weak one (8 of 20 doubtful, fragmentary).

texts.label: “San Francisco” table: 5 telegrams read by Brice Dudout (18 September 1914 - 22 April 1916)
texts.summary: San Francisco → “Dr Sunwen”, Tokyo, October 1915–April 1916; signed 森 (Lin Sen). Table published by D. Bourdeau. Also attested on 18 September 1914.

reading_review.note: 5 telegrams (Lin Sen; Sun's 22 April decision to return), 0128, 0274, 0436 clean, 0624b clean after a garbled opening; 0630b is fragmentary ({麾}{舠}{春}...{宬}...{帀}).

texts.label: “Honolulu” table, “Aloha” alphabet: 2 telegrams read by Brice Dudout (30 April 1916 - 16 May 1916)
texts.summary: Honolulu → Tokyo, 30 April and 16 May 1916; indicator “Aloha”. Grid published by D. Bourdeau, written here with an alphabet without q and with w (23 October 2026).

reading_review.note: 2 short Wu Tiecheng telegrams; 0011b clean, 0054b reads except its 6-character tail ({贛}{箬}定{吟}電{復}; {復} is a proposed emendation of the decoded 螂), left as a gap in the translation.
